text:
infra-bot: ALERT: Spike in 502/504 responses from euc2b ALB pool starting ~2439999580. Rate ~120 5xx/min, error traces show downstream Envoy resets and NLB target flaps. Tags: customer-impact, high-latency, sessions

sima: paging oncall-ops, I'm seeing a cluster of sessions pinned to targets in AZ-c that are reporting high retransmits. stack: frontend-alb -> envoy -> model-nodes (nvidia-pool-euc2b).

nate: oncall-ops here, joining. Thanks infra-bot. Any perf/scale changes recently?

sima: no deploys in the last hour. No infra changes I can see. Cloud shows AZ-c partial reachability loss (packet drops). ALB healthchecks start failing for one target group, NLB marks targets unhealthy then healthy repeatedly.

sophie: I'm taking IC. Quick triage checklist: 1) customer impact scope 2) isolate region, 3) temporary mitigation (traffic steering) 4) root cause hypothesis.

kevin: customer impact - Sent SRE dashboard link to support. Early traces show sessions long-lived (session affinity enabled on ALB). Customers with sticky sessions report 5xx during retries. Likely session-affinity exacerbating targeting unstable nodes.

maria: can we temporarily disable ALB stickiness for the affected target group? That should distribute new sessions. Risk: some clients rely on affinity. Thoughts?

sophie: do it as a quick mitigation, but gate with a small TTL change and call it out in status. Nate, can you make the change and watch?

nate: doing now. Command: ```aws elbv2 modify-target-group-attributes --target-group-arn arn:aws:...:tg/frontend-euc2b --attributes Key=stickiness.enabled,Value=false```

nate: applied. ALB stickiness disabled for tg/frontend-euc2b. Monitoring.

infra-bot: Event: stickiness update accepted by AWS, propagation ~20s.

sima: seeing immediate reduction in per-target queue depth for the previously pinned targets. 5xx rate dropping to ~40/min. Not back to baseline yet.

kevin: good. Also, Envoy keepalive between ALB and envoys are low; clients keep retrying and hitting transient errors. We should bump Envoy upstream timeout as a soft mitigation to drop stuck connections earlier.

maria: suggest bump upstream idle_timeout to 20s in envoy-proxy config for euc2 cluster. That will close stale connections faster and allow LB to reassign.

nate: applying envoy config change to canary group (10% hosts) first: ```kubectl apply -f envoy-timeout-canary.yaml``` then roll if stable.

sophie: while that rolls, let's route a fraction of traffic away from euc2b to euc1 (weighted routing). Ops playbook allows 30% shift without global impact. Who can run the Route53 change?

maria: I can. Route53 weight adjustments: update record set frontend.api.redwood.ai weight euc2b=70 euc1=30 -> euc2b=40 euc1=60. Doing it now.

maria: Route53 change in progress (change-id: Z12345). TTL was 60s.

infra-bot: DNS change propagated to global resolvers in ~45s per our checks.

sima: metrics: frontend 5xx overall down 65% after stickiness off + partial traffic shift. Some customer sessions still failing if they hit problematic AZ-c nodes.

nate: going to cordon and drain the 4 nodes in AZ-c showing high retransmit counters: ```kubectl cordon node/euc2b-node-12 && kubectl drain node/euc2b-node-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data``` repeating for node-13/14/15.

kevin: make sure to set rollout policy to not kill cache-heavy nodes all at once; use rolling drain at 1 node at a time. KV-cache is warm on some targets.

nate: draining node-12 -> pods relocating. Healthchecks for tg update to healthy as targets warm elsewhere.

sophie: assign post-mortem owner: sima. Keep timeline and customer-impact notes. Escalate to networking team for AZ-c link degradation.

maria: notif to customers: drafting status update. We should highlight mitigations (disabled stickiness, traffic shift, node drain) and expected timeline for full recovery.

incident-bot: Incident created INC-2026-2439, status: investigating, severity: SEV2, assigned: oncall-ops, postmortem-owner: sima.

sima: small update: Net team confirms intermittent fiber flaps in AZ-c causing asymmetric routing; cloud provider working on patch to spine switch. Estimated time to fix 2 hours.

kevin: given provider ETA, recommend keeping stickiness off for 4 hours and maintain traffic weighting until provider confirms stable. Also recommend temporary increase to API retry jitter to reduce thundering retries.

nate: changed client-side retry config in edge-proxy canary to add jitter (0-300ms) and max-retries=2. Rolling to 10% first.

sophie: handoff plan: I will remain IC for next 45 minutes then hand to sima for monitoring overnight if provider still has work. Assign oncall-ops to perform hourly check-ins.

maria: status message posted to customers with link to incident page. :loudspeaker:

infra-bot: Monitoring shows 5xx baseline nearing normal: 502/min -> 8/min.

sima: leaving detailed notes in the incident doc (INC-2026-2439). Will draft RCA once provider confirms root cause. Thanks team.

oncall-ops: acknowledging handoff. Setting reminder for hourly check-ins and watch windows.

sophie: closing active mitigation steps; keep incident open until provider confirms AZ-c fix. Good job everyone. :thumbsup:
